video_title: Scaling Laws: Algorithmic Disgorgement with Christina Lee
transcript: Christina, welcome to Scaling Laws. >> Thank you. I'm really excited to be here. >> So, I'm always on the hunt for folks who are diving into areas of AI policy and AI legal issues that perhaps are being underinvestigated and aren't rising to the four of popular discourse. So instead of just saying like don't use this model or just delete the data that you've already trained this model on, just say get rid of the whole model. >> So something wrong with it from a legal standpoint. Uh, that would obviously be incredibly costly. So, where did we see this remedy start to emerge and why was it something that the FTC felt was warranted in that context? >> Yeah, for sure. So the first um instance that we know of algorithmic discoursement being um ordered um through a um government agency is the FTC settlement with Cambridge Analytica. Um that was back in 2019. So it's been a few years already, right? Um and so as many people probably remember um there was a whole scandal with Cambridge Analytica and one of the things that um the FTC alleged was that when Cambridge Analytica collected all the data from Facebook users um for what they ended up making the psychoraphic mo um profiles of voters um the app that they used on Facebook said that they weren't going to collect any personally identifiable information. So none of your identifying information is going to be collected through this app. We're just interested in demographic level information. But the app itself actually did collect personally identifiable information like if your Facebook user ID and so on and so forth. So the FTC said that is deceptive. Um you said you weren't going to do this, you did this thing, right? And so all um all of the data that you collected was through deceptive actual practices which is prohibited under the FTC act. Um and so what um what the FTC did there, what the innovation there was is you could um in past FTC settlements um regarding deceptive data collection um usually the the remedy was delete the data.
